subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should `getAcpSessionManager()` preserve its shipped class identity while its session-returning methods are projected, or may this release intentionally replace it with a structural facade?
rationale: Sealing core recovery state is necessary, but choosing whether to break a released third-party Plugin SDK identity contract is a maintainer-owned security and compatibility decision.

options.title: Preserve identity, project methods
options.body: Keep the released manager identity and move raw session access behind internal-only methods so public manager results use the safe projection.

options.title: Approve immediate facade break
options.body: Accept the null-prototype facade as an intentional incompatible Plugin SDK change and document the exact upgrade impact for plugin authors.

options.title: Introduce a versioned transition
options.body: Add a new safe facade getter and schedule removal of the old class-returning contract through an explicit deprecation or major-version path.

recommendation.title: Preserve identity, project methods
recommendation.body: Keep the released manager identity and move raw session access behind internal-only methods so public manager results use the safe projection.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP seam history makes this the strongest available owner for deciding the permanent public boundary.
